embodiment_body_ownership.evidence: The tool hand is visibly continuous through its wrist and forearm into the screen-right sleeve, and the detached assembly is clearly robot-owned. The support fingers/palm at approximately x570-774,y681-816 and thumb x660-727,y590-633 contact the bare mid-frame. The support sleeve/skin patch at x491-592,y550-590 disappears behind the top rail and internal actuator; the complete support wrist-to-forearm contour is not traceable together. This required route is unobservable, not evidence of a hidden deformity.

embodiment_joint_chain_and_reach.evidence: The robot upper segment, large circular elbow at x192-425,y509-744, open frame x408-1009,y573-787 and separate wrist near x1006-1119,y692-830 form a distinct connected mechanical chain. The driver reach is clear. However the frozen complete human support-hand wrist/forearm route is partly behind the frame, so the complete combined joint/reach check cannot pass despite the robot-specific chain passing.

embodiment_support_and_balance.evidence: The detached mechanical arm rests on two dark padded cradle blocks, approximately x170-499,y727-850 under the elbow and x748-1012,y780-867 under the distal frame, over a towel on the workbench. The support hand stabilizes the frame; it is not portrayed as carrying the whole limb. These consequential support contacts are visible. Human lower-body support is ordinary off-frame context, not an added test.

embodiment_contact_and_space.evidence: The screen-right tool fingers grip a single driver; its shaft extends visibly to a seated tip in the circular fastener at the proximal wrist/hand mounting area around x1148,y707. The other hand curls fingers under the near bare forearm rail between the elbow and wrist, with the thumb over the rail and open internal space framing the contact. It contacts the mid-frame, not the robot palm or distal wrist. The visible skin/tool/metal contact boundaries are distinct; this local contact pass does not establish the hidden support wrist route.

embodiment_visibility_and_projection.evidence: The face/hair, robot chassis, two work hands, whole detached robot arm, separate elbow/frame/wrist and driver endpoint all share the original frame, and the repaired machine/contact details are readable. The support wrist-to-forearm route required by the explicit continuity clause remains partly behind the mechanical rail/actuator. Whole-scene visibility therefore fails even though the targeted robot and contact components are visible.
